context: small plant · fast to build; permits, foundations, calibration and mix approvals govern

brief.intro: New to this project type? A ready-mix plant weighs aggregates, cement, water and admixtures, mixes them and loads truck mixers. It is a compact, largely factory-made machine: aggregate bins fed by a ramp or conveyor, cement silos, a weighing and mixing tower, a control cabin, and around it a yard with wash-out pits, water recycling, a laboratory and truck parking. Erection takes weeks, not months. What takes time is everything around it — the environmental and operating permits, the foundations and aggregate bays, the power and water supply, and then calibration of the scales and approval of the concrete mixes by the customers or the authority before the first cubic metre can be sold.

scope.name: Site preparation & enabling
scope.desc: Grading, access roads, temporary facilities and underground services.

scope.name: Building & machine foundations
scope.desc: Column footings plus the heavy bases, pits and trenches the machines sit on — set out from the equipment drawings.

scope.name: Steel structure & envelope
scope.desc: Portal frames, crane beams, roof and wall cladding, making the hall weather-tight.

scope.name: Industrial floor
scope.desc: Flat, hard-wearing floor slab, cast after the roof is on and before the machines move in.

scope.name: Aggregate bays & feeding
scope.desc: Ground bays, loading ramp or hopper, and inclined belt conveyor to the bins.

scope.name: Aggregate bins & weighing
scope.desc: Overhead bins with weigh belt or weigh hoppers.

scope.name: Cement silos & screw conveyors
scope.desc: Silos with filters, level probes and screw feeders.

scope.name: Mixing tower
scope.desc: Mixer, water and admixture dosing, discharge chute to trucks.

scope.name: Control cabin & automation
scope.desc: Batching computer, scales and ticket printing.

scope.name: Water system & recycling
scope.desc: Water tanks, chiller or ice plant in hot climates, wash-out and reclaim pits.

scope.name: Plant utilities
scope.desc: Compressed air, Water supply & recycling, Chilled water / ice (hot climates), Dust collection — the services every machine needs before it can run.

scope.name: Power supply & control
scope.desc: Substation, transformers, switchgear, cabling and the plant control system.

scope.name: Fire protection, HVAC & dust / fume extraction
scope.desc: Life-safety and environmental systems required for the operating permit.

scope.name: Commissioning & ramp-up
scope.desc: Scale calibration, trial mixes for every concrete grade, and mix approval by the customers / authority.

glossary.plain: weighing out the exact amount of each ingredient for a load of concrete.
the machine that mixes the batch before it is discharged into the truck.
a wet plant mixes in its own mixer; a dry plant only weighs and the truck mixes.
a hopper on load cells that weighs the material inside it.
a chemical added in small doses to change how the concrete behaves.
equipment that washes leftover concrete and recovers the aggregates and water.
a test batch made to prove a mix design reaches its strength and workability.
checking every scale against known weights so batches are accurate; usually witnessed and certified.

must_get_right: Start the environmental and operating permits first — they are longer than the construction.
Foundations, silo bases and the truck-loading point follow the plant supplier's drawings; get them early.
Power, water and the access road must be ready before commissioning; a plant with no water cannot be tested.
Leave time after erection for calibration, trial mixes and 28-day (or accelerated) strength results before production is counted on.

basis_of_planning.standard: AACE Recommended Practice 38R-06 — Documenting the Schedule Basis

sections.heading: Scheduling method & tools
sections.body: A Critical Path Method (CPM) network built in Primavera P6, developed to a Level 3 control schedule with retained-logic progress. Activities are organised by plant area along the process line and by discipline, with every long-lead machine tracked from order to factory test, shipping and arrival.

sections.heading: Calendars & working time
sections.body: Standard site calendar for construction; equipment installation may run extended shifts under vendor supervision. Commissioning follows the vendor's programme, and hot commissioning runs continuously once started.

sections.heading: Sequencing logic & critical path
sections.body: Permits and supplier drawings → foundations, bays and pits → plant erection → power, water and air → calibration → trial mixes → mix approval → production. The critical path usually runs through the permits or the plant delivery, then mix approval.

sections.heading: Key assumptions
sections.body: The process technology and vendor are fixed before design starts; vendor drawings for foundations arrive on the agreed dates; permanent power and water are available before cold commissioning; raw material for trial production is on site.

sections.body: The schedule tracks the following as milestones because they drive the programme:

sections.heading: Access, resource & site constraints
sections.body: Heavy machines need crane access and often must enter before the cladding or a wall is closed. Vendor supervisors are booked for fixed periods. Clean, dry, powered conditions are required before precision equipment is unpacked.

sections.heading: Risks, float & contingency
sections.body: Main risks: permit delay, late power or water connection, calibration failures, and trial mixes not reaching strength. Contingency is held before the first contracted delivery date.

sections.heading: Schedule levels of detail
sections.body: Reported at Level 1 (milestones) and Level 2 (summary) to the client; controlled at Level 3 by plant area and discipline; expanded to Level 4–5 lookahead for the installation crews and the vendor supervisors — consistent with AACE 37R-06.
